facts.fact: The current pip supports CPython 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 and 3.15 plus the latest PyPy3; Python 2 and older Python 3 versions are not supported.
PyPI no longer supports `pip search` (XML-RPC search); users must search PyPI via the website instead.
facts.source_quote: PyPI no longer supports ``pip search`` (or XML-RPC search). Please use https://pypi.org/search (via a browser)

facts.fact: pip's backtracking (2020) resolver is the default; the legacy resolver (--use-deprecated=legacy-resolver) is deprecated and unsupported.
facts.source_quote: The legacy resolver is deprecated and unsupported.

facts.fact: When installing a project from a local directory, pip builds it in place rather than copying it to a temporary directory first (out-of-tree builds were removed in 22.1).
facts.source_quote: When provided with a project that's in a local directory, pip will invoke the build system "in place".

When building from such a path, pip first copies the project into a temporary directory and runs the build backend there, leaving the original source tree untouched.
Support for Python 2.7 ended with the pip 20.3 series; pip 21.0, released in January 2021, was the first release to require Python 3.
Pip first shipped this backtracking resolver as its default in version 20.3, released in November 2020.
